paragraphs.text: translated by
1. LET these speak loudly forth; let us speak out aloud: to the loud speaking Pressing-stones address the speech;
paragraphs.original: प्रैते वदन्तु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यो वाचं वदता वदद्भ्यः ।
paragraphs.translit: praite vadantu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyo vācaṃ vadatā vadadbhyaḥ |

paragraphs.text: When, rich with Soma juice, Stones of the mountain, ye, united, swift to Indra bring the sound of praise.
paragraphs.original: यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः श्लोकं घोषं भरथेन्द्राय सोमिनः
paragraphs.translit: yadadrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākamāśavaḥ ślokaṃ ghoṣaṃ bharathendrāya sominaḥ

paragraphs.text: 2. They speak out like a hundred, like a thousand men: they cry aloud to us with their green-tinted mouths,
paragraphs.original: एते वदन्ति शतवत्सहस्रवदभि क्रन्दन्ति हरितेभिरासभिः ।
paragraphs.translit: ete vadanti śatavatsahasravadabhi krandanti haritebhirāsabhiḥ |

paragraphs.text: While, pious Stones, they ply their task with piety, and, even before the Hotar, taste the offered food.
paragraphs.original: विष्ट्वी ग्रावाणः सुकृतः सुकृत्यया होतुश्चित्पूर्वे हविरद्यमाशत
paragraphs.translit: viṣṭvī grāvāṇaḥ sukṛtaḥ sukṛtyayā hotuścitpūrve haviradyamāśata

paragraphs.text: 3. Loudly they speak, for they have found the savoury meath: they make a humming sound over the meat prepared.
paragraphs.original: एते वदन्त्यविदन्नना मधु न्यूङ्खयन्ते अधि पक्व आमिषि ।
paragraphs.translit: ete vadantyavidannanā madhu nyūṅkhayante adhi pakva āmiṣi |

paragraphs.text: As they devour the branch of the Red-coloured Tree, these, the well-pastured Bulls, have uttered bellowings.
paragraphs.original: वृक्षस्य शाखामरुणस्य बप्सतस्ते सूभर्वा वृषभाः प्रेमराविषुः
paragraphs.translit: vṛkṣasya śākhāmaruṇasya bapsataste sūbharvā vṛṣabhāḥ premarāviṣuḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. They cry aloud, with strong exhilarating drink, calling on Indra now, for they have found the meath.
paragraphs.original: बृहद्वदन्ति मदिरेण मन्दिनेन्द्रं क्रोशन्तोऽविदन्नना मधु ।
paragraphs.translit: bṛhadvadanti madireṇa mandinendraṃ krośanto'vidannanā madhu |

paragraphs.text: Bold, with the sisters they have danced, embraced by them, making the earth reecho with their ringing sound.
paragraphs.original: संरभ्या धीराः स्वसृभिरनर्तिषुराघोषयन्तः पृथिवीमुपब्दिभिः
paragraphs.translit: saṃrabhyā dhīrāḥ svasṛbhiranartiṣurāghoṣayantaḥ pṛthivīmupabdibhiḥ

paragraphs.text: 5. The Eagles have sent forth their cry aloft in heaven; in the sky's vault the dark impetuous ones have danced.
paragraphs.original: सुपर्णा वाचमक्रतोप द्यव्याखरे कृष्णा इषिरा अनर्तिषुः ।
paragraphs.translit: suparṇā vācamakratopa dyavyākhare kṛṣṇā iṣirā anartiṣuḥ |

paragraphs.text: Then downward to the nether stone's fixt place they sink, and, splendid as the Sun, effuse their copious stream.
paragraphs.original: न्यङ्नि यन्त्युपरस्य निष्कृतं पुरू रेतो दधिरे सूर्यश्वितः
paragraphs.translit: nyaṅni yantyuparasya niṣkṛtaṃ purū reto dadhire sūryaśvitaḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. Like strong ones drawing, they have put forth all their strength: the Bulls, harnessed together, bear the chariot-poles.
paragraphs.original: उग्रा इव प्रवहन्तः समायमुः साकं युक्ता वृषणो बिभ्रतो धुरः ।
paragraphs.translit: ugrā iva pravahantaḥ samāyamuḥ sākaṃ yuktā vṛṣaṇo bibhrato dhuraḥ |

paragraphs.text: When they have bellowed, panting, swallowing their food, the sound of their loud snorting is like that of steeds.
paragraphs.original: यच्छ्वसन्तो जग्रसाना अराविषुः शृण्व एषां प्रोथथो अर्वतामिव
paragraphs.translit: yacchvasanto jagrasānā arāviṣuḥ śṛṇva eṣāṃ prothatho arvatāmiva

paragraphs.text: 7. To these who have ten workers and a tenfold girth, to these who have ten yoke-straps and ten binding thongs,
paragraphs.original: दशावनिभ्यो दशकक्ष्येभ्यो दशयोक्त्रेभ्यो दशयोजनेभ्यः ।
paragraphs.translit: daśāvanibhyo daśakakṣyebhyo daśayoktrebhyo daśayojanebhyaḥ |

paragraphs.text: To these who bear ten reins, the eternal, sing ye praise, to these who bear ten car-poles, ten when they are yoked.
paragraphs.original: दशाभीशुभ्यो अर्चताजरेभ्यो दश धुरो दश युक्ता वहद्भ्यः
paragraphs.translit: daśābhīśubhyo arcatājarebhyo daśa dhuro daśa yuktā vahadbhyaḥ

paragraphs.text: 8. These Stones with ten conductors, rapid in their course, with lovely revolution travel round and round.
paragraphs.original: ते अद्रयो दशयन्त्रास आशवस्तेषामाधानं पर्येति हर्यतम् ।
paragraphs.translit: te adrayo daśayantrāsa āśavasteṣāmādhānaṃ paryeti haryatam |

paragraphs.text: They have been first to drink the flowing Soma juice, first to enjoy the milky fluid of the stalk.
paragraphs.original: त ऊ सुतस्य सोम्यस्यान्धसोऽंशोः पीयूषं प्रथमस्य भेजिरे
paragraphs.translit: ta ū sutasya somyasyāndhaso'ṃśoḥ pīyūṣaṃ prathamasya bhejire

paragraphs.text: 9. These Soma-eaters kiss Indra's Bay-coloured Steeds: draining. the stalk they sit upon the ox's hide.
paragraphs.original: ते सोमादो हरी इन्द्रस्य निंसतेऽंशुं दुहन्तो अध्यासते गवि ।
paragraphs.translit: te somādo harī indrasya niṃsate'ṃśuṃ duhanto adhyāsate gavi |

paragraphs.text: Indra, when he hath drunk Soma-nicath drawn by them, waxes in strength, is famed, is mighty as a Bull.
paragraphs.original: तेभिर्दुग्धं पपिवान्सोम्यं मध्विन्द्रो वर्धते प्रथते वृषायते
paragraphs.translit: tebhirdugdhaṃ papivānsomyaṃ madhvindro vardhate prathate vṛṣāyate

paragraphs.text: 10. Strong is your stalk; ye, verily, never shall be harmed; ye have refreshment, ye are ever satisfied.
paragraphs.original: वृषा वो अंशुर्न किला रिषाथनेळावन्तः सदमित्स्थनाशिताः ।
paragraphs.translit: vṛṣā vo aṃśurna kilā riṣāthaneḷāvantaḥ sadamitsthanāśitāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Fair are ye, as it were, through splendour of his wealth, his in whose sacrifice, O Stones, ye find delight.
paragraphs.original: रैवत्येव महसा चारव स्थन यस्य ग्रावाणो अजुषध्वमध्वरम्
paragraphs.translit: raivatyeva mahasā cārava sthana yasya grāvāṇo ajuṣadhvamadhvaram

paragraphs.text: 11. Bored deep, but not pierced through with holes, are ye, O Stones, not loosened, never weary, and exempt from death,
paragraphs.original: तृदिला अतृदिलासो अद्रयोऽश्रमणा अशृथिता अमृत्यवः ।
paragraphs.translit: tṛdilā atṛdilāso adrayo'śramaṇā aśṛthitā amṛtyavaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Eternal, undiseased, moving in sundry ways, unthirsting, full of fatness, void of all desire.
paragraphs.original: अनातुरा अजरा स्थामविष्णवः सुपीवसो अतृषिता अतृष्णजः
paragraphs.translit: anāturā ajarā sthāmaviṣṇavaḥ supīvaso atṛṣitā atṛṣṇajaḥ

paragraphs.text: 12. Your fathers, verily, stand firm from age to age: they, loving rest, are not dissevered from their seat.
paragraphs.original: ध्रुवा एव वः पितरो युगेयुगे क्षेमकामासः सदसो न युञ्जते ।
paragraphs.translit: dhruvā eva vaḥ pitaro yugeyuge kṣemakāmāsaḥ sadaso na yuñjate |

paragraphs.text: Untouched by time, ne'er lacking green plants and green trees, they with their voice have caused the heavens and earth to hear.
paragraphs.original: अजुर्यासो हरिषाचो हरिद्रव आ द्यां रवेण पृथिवीमशुश्रवुः
paragraphs.translit: ajuryāso hariṣāco haridrava ā dyāṃ raveṇa pṛthivīmaśuśravuḥ

paragraphs.text: 13. This, this the Stones proclaim, what time they are disjoined, and when with ringing sounds they move and drink the balm.
paragraphs.original: तदिद्वदन्त्यद्रयो विमोचने यामन्नञ्जस्पा इव घेदुपब्दिभिः ।
paragraphs.translit: tadidvadantyadrayo vimocane yāmannañjaspā iva ghedupabdibhiḥ |

paragraphs.text: Like tillers of the ground when they are sowing seed, they mix the Soma, nor, devouring, diminish it.
paragraphs.original: वपन्तो बीजमिव धान्याकृतः पृञ्चन्ति सोमं न मिनन्ति बप्सतः
paragraphs.translit: vapanto bījamiva dhānyākṛtaḥ pṛñcanti somaṃ na minanti bapsataḥ

paragraphs.text: 14. They have raised high their voice for juice, for sacrifice, striking the Mother earth as though they danced thereon.
paragraphs.original: सुते अध्वरे अधि वाचमक्रता क्रीळयो न मातरं तुदन्तः ।
paragraphs.translit: sute adhvare adhi vācamakratā krīḷayo na mātaraṃ tudantaḥ |

paragraphs.text: So loose thou too his thought who hath effused the sap, and let the Stones which we are honouring be disjoined.
paragraphs.original: वि षू मुञ्चा सुषुवुषो मनीषां वि वर्तन्तामद्रयश्चायमानाः
paragraphs.translit: vi ṣū muñcā suṣuvuṣo manīṣāṃ vi vartantāmadrayaścāyamānāḥ
